sections.html:
Henrico wraps around Richmond on the west, north and east, with the James River and the city to the south. It has no incorporated town, so Laurel, an unincorporated place, serves as the seat of government. The 2020 census counted 334,389 people, and the 2025 estimate is 342,775.

There were 140,739 housing units in 2020 and 4.6% were vacant. Owners occupy 62.7% of homes and renters 37.3%.

Renters fill more than a third of occupied homes, which means many Henrico sellers are letting go of a former rental, along with tenants, overdue repairs or both. The county is old, dating to 1611, and a Henrico house can be almost any age, so know the year built before you compare it with a neighbor's sale. Henrico also maintains its own roads rather than leaving them to the state, so a problem road next to your lot goes to the county.

The county revalues each parcel yearly, at 100 percent of fair market value, and the figure takes effect January 1. The Real Estate Assessment Division, part of the Department of Finance, works from recorded deeds and the sale prices that buyers, sellers and agents report.

Staff compare sale prices with assessed values, and a neighborhood is picked for reassessment when its ratio sits well above or below 100 percent. For houses the division generally uses the sales comparison approach, adjusting for size, quality, condition and location.

Notices are mailed beginning in February. Tax bills often go straight to the mortgage company, so an owner with an escrow account may never see the notice unless the lender forwards it; look up your value on the division's page at henrico.gov.

Start by applying for reconsideration. State law makes April 1 of the current year the final filing day. Call 804-501-4300 or write to AssessmentAppeal@henrico.gov for forms.

Reconsideration fits when the value exceeds fair market value, rests on wrong property information, or is inequitable against similar properties. Staff inspect the property, tell you the value they recommend and send the case to the Board of Real Estate Review and Equalization. If you still disagree, you may appear before the board.

Virginia's burden rule applies at the hearing, so bring comparable sales and evidence of condition. Filing an administrative appeal within 90 days of the assessment keeps the bill from counting as delinquent while it is pending and for 30 days following the decision.

InstallmentDueWhere to pay
First halfOn or before June 5Treasury, 4301 E. Parham Road or 3820 Nine Mile Road
Second halfOn or before December 5Same offices, weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., holidays excluded

The Treasury Division bills real estate and personal property tax and collects it, delinquent balances included, under County Code section 20-108. Ask Treasury for current penalty and interest before you plan a payoff.

The assessment page lists relief programs: partial exemptions for certain residential, multifamily and commercial properties, an exemption for qualified owners with a service-connected disability and their surviving spouses, the Real Estate Advantage Program for owners 65 or older or disabled with an April 1 filing deadline, and a Land Use program with a November 1 application date. For the Advantage program call 804-501-4263.

Because Henrico reassesses annually, the value on your February notice is a snapshot as of January 1. A repair finished in March will not change that year's figure, and neither will a sale that closes after the snapshot. When you price the house, compare the assessed value with what comparable Henrico homes actually sold for, because the division itself checks assessments against sale prices and moves neighborhoods whose ratio drifts.

If the notice lists wrong square footage, bedrooms or a finished basement that does not exist, that is incorrect property information and a clean basis for reconsideration. Photograph the problem and measure it before you call.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the two installments
sections.html:
With payments due June 5 and December 5, think about where your closing falls. Close in late spring and the first half is nearly due; the settlement statement shows how it is divided with the buyer. Close in autumn and the first half is typically paid already, so the buyer reimburses you for the months after closing. Request the agent's proration worksheet and check it against your contract.

If your lender pays tax from escrow, ask the servicer which installment it has paid, since the escrow refund after payoff is separate from the closing proceeds. Take photo ID, parcel details and recent bills to the title company. Treasury can confirm payment in writing if the agent asks for proof.

A sale after bills go out has its own rule. The treasurer may cancel the prior owner's bill and reissue it to the buyer, and paying within two weeks of the new notice avoids any penalty on that assessment.

If you are behind, ask Treasury for a written payoff that states the date it is good through. Pass it to the title company for payment at closing, and find out whether an exemption or Land Use status on the parcel ends with the sale.

  1. Request the written payoff and its good-through date.
  2. Check your assessment notice, and file for reconsideration by April 1 if the value looks wrong.
  3. Tell tenants, if any, about showings and move-out timing.
  4. Confirm payment with Treasury after closing.

sections.h2: What Henrico buyers and inspectors look at
sections.html:
Neighborhood names matter to buyers. The county's census-designated places include Short Pump, Glen Allen, Innsbrook, Tuckahoe, Sandston, Lakeside and Highland Springs, and each draws a different crowd, so tell your buyer which one your address really belongs to. Fair Oaks and Varina are other named communities.

Henrico's humid climate, with about 50 days above 90 degrees and 88 days with lows below freezing in an average year, puts attention on roofs, gutters and crawl space moisture. Keep repair receipts. Buyers also look at access: Interstates 64, 95, 195 and 295 all cross the county, Richmond International Airport is in the east, and Amtrak's Staples Mill Road station is in Henrico. Short Pump, Glen Allen, Tuckahoe and Highland Springs each have a different feel, so describe your own area honestly.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or a house that needs work
sections.html: Cash Home Buyers can review a Henrico house as is, including a rental with tenants or a house with unpaid tax, and send a written cash offer without obligation. Selling for cash avoids repairs and a buyer's loan approval. The tax rules are the same for every buyer, though, and any balance is paid from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Henrico County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment is due on or before June 5 and the second on or before December 5.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Henrico County real estate assessment?
faqs.a: By law, appeals must be filed no later than April 1 of the current year. Call 804-501-4300 or email AssessmentAppeal@henrico.gov for a form.

faqs.q: Does Henrico County reassess every year?
faqs.a: Yes. The Real Estate Assessment Division reassesses all real property effective January 1 each year and mails notices beginning in February.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Henrico County tax in person?
faqs.a: Treasury has offices at 4301 E. Parham Road and 3820 Nine Mile Road, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding holidays.

faqs.q: Is there tax relief for older Henrico County homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. The Real Estate Advantage Program serves owners who are 65 or older or disabled and meet other criteria, with an April 1 filing deadline. Call 804-501-4263 for details.
